overview.summary: A rapid lead-hand linear strike designed to reach a target through an efficient path while preserving structural alignment, balance, defensive coverage, mobility, and rapid recovery.
objectives: Move the lead hand toward the target with minimal unnecessary displacement.
Use a direct, efficient hand path with limited lateral deviation.
Keep the non-striking hand in its defensive reference position.
Keep the center of mass supported by a controllable base.
Preserve mobility and readiness for another action.
Avoid unnecessary tension, overextension, and joint loading.
Return efficiently to a defensively useful state.

principles.title: Direct hand path
principles.explanation: The lead fist travels forward with minimal unnecessary sideways movement. A shorter path generally makes the action easier to control and retract.

principles.title: Controlled elbow extension
principles.explanation: The elbow extends behind the fist while remaining short of a forceful lock. The wrist, elbow, and shoulder should support the direction of the strike.

principles.title: Stable base
principles.explanation: The stance supports the movement while the torso stays controlled. Reaching with the upper body can move the body beyond its comfortable base of support.

principles.title: Coordinated movement
principles.explanation: The fist, elbow, shoulder, torso, and stance contribute as a sequence rather than as isolated parts. The goal is efficient timing, not unnecessary tension.

principles.title: Immediate recovery
principles.explanation: After extension, the fist returns along a controlled path and the guard is restored. Recovery is part of the technique, not an action added afterward.

principles.title: How to interpret force
principles.explanation: Punching force depends on mass, acceleration, timing, contact, and whole-body coordination. A camera can describe visible motion but does not directly measure impact force or joint torque.

principles.title: Biomechanics
principles.explanation: The body segments work together to produce and control the strike. Reference positions are variables that support functional goals.

principles.title: Stability
principles.explanation: A stable base resists unwanted loss of control while preserving the ability to move again.

principles.title: Mobility
principles.explanation: A useful position leaves enough freedom to evade, continue, defend, or change direction.

principles.title: Defensive coverage
principles.explanation: The non-striking side and body position should limit unnecessary exposed area while the striking limb is committed.

principles.title: Exposure
principles.explanation: Exposure is the vulnerable area and duration created by the movement. Efficient technique limits both.

principles.title: Energy efficiency
principles.explanation: A useful solution avoids unnecessary tension, wind-up, and body displacement.

principles.title: Joint safety
principles.explanation: Useful reach is preferred over maximum possible extension so the joints remain controlled and recovery stays available.

principles.title: Temporal efficiency
principles.explanation: Each phase should happen in a useful sequence, with recovery beginning promptly after peak reach.

learning_content.purpose: Build a direct, controlled lead-hand punch that returns to a reliable guard.

guard-stance.goal: Establish a balanced and defensively useful ready state that allows striking, defending, moving, or recovering efficiently.
key_cues: Keep the non-striking side defensively useful.
Keep visual attention toward the target.
guard-stance.remember: A good jab begins with a quiet, ready guard.
guard-stance.why_it_matters: A functional ready state reduces the movement needed for the next action without forcing one traditional pose.
guard-stance.transition_condition: Begin extension when the base and non-striking hand are stable enough to move without losing readiness.

extend-the-lead-jab.goal: Accelerate the lead hand toward the target through an efficient path while maintaining whole-body control.
key_cues: Move the lead fist directly toward the target.
Let the shoulder coordinate with the arm without shrugging.
Keep the elbow controlled behind the fist.
Keep the rear hand protecting the guard.
Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.
extend-the-lead-jab.remember: The jab is direct and controlled, not a reach or a forceful lock.
extend-the-lead-jab.why_it_matters: The measurable joint and trajectory references support a useful strike; they are evidence for the movement objective, not the objective itself.
extend-the-lead-jab.transition_condition: Move to peak reach when the hand has reached the useful target path without losing alignment or balance.

retract-to-guard.goal: Return the striking limb efficiently and finish in a stable state that permits the next action.
key_cues: Retract the lead hand immediately after extension.
Bring the hand back to its guard position.
Keep the base stable while recovering.
Do not let the rear hand or posture drift.
retract-to-guard.remember: Recovery is part of the jab, not an action added afterward.
avoid: Holding the hand away from guard
retract-to-guard.why_it_matters: Recovery means returning to a useful functional state; it does not require identical coordinates to the starting reference.
retract-to-guard.transition_condition: Finish when balance, defensive coverage, and mobility are restored enough for the next action.

common_errors.title: Rear hand drops
common_errors.description: The rear hand leaves the guard while the lead hand moves.
common_errors.why: This leaves the head less protected and breaks the intended coordination.
common_errors.correction: Keep the rear hand home and rehearse the jab slowly.

common_errors.title: Excessive forward lean
common_errors.description: The upper body reaches beyond the base to make the fist travel farther.
common_errors.why: The stance becomes less stable and recovery takes longer.
common_errors.correction: Move the fist along a direct path while keeping the base underneath you.

common_errors.title: Elbow flares
common_errors.description: The elbow travels sideways instead of staying behind the fist.
common_errors.why: The path becomes longer and alignment becomes harder to control.
common_errors.correction: Keep the elbow controlled and let the shoulder coordinate the extension.

common_errors.title: Forceful elbow lock
common_errors.description: The elbow is snapped straight at full extension.
common_errors.why: This can create unnecessary joint stress and tension.
common_errors.correction: Reach under control and stop short of a forceful lock.

common_errors.title: Wrist misalignment
common_errors.description: The wrist bends away from the forearm at the end of the punch.
common_errors.why: The hand, wrist, and forearm no longer support the direction of the strike.
common_errors.correction: Keep the wrist aligned and reduce speed until the shape is consistent.

common_errors.title: Slow recovery
common_errors.description: The lead hand stays away from the guard after reaching the target.
common_errors.why: The technique remains unfinished and the guard is exposed.
common_errors.correction: Make the return immediate, smooth, and controlled.

knowledge_check.question: What should the rear hand do while the lead hand extends?
knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: the rear hand protects the guard throughout the jab.

knowledge_check.question: What should happen after peak extension?

options.label: Hold the hand away from the guard
Retract the lead hand toward guard

knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: recovery is an immediate part of the technique.

knowledge_check.question: What is a good jab path?
knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: the lead fist travels directly toward the target.

knowledge_check.question: Should the elbow be forcefully locked?
knowledge_check.feedback: Correct: keep the elbow controlled and avoid a forceful lock.

rounds: Guard: settle the base and protect the head.
Initiate and extend: send the lead fist directly toward the target.
Reach and recover: stop short of a forceful lock, then return promptly to guard.
shadow_rehearsal.instruction: Complete 3 slow rounds, then increase speed only if the path, guard, and recovery stay consistent.
